Mordheim:  Revenge of the Warbands

Seven years, four months, and three days after the destruction of Mordheim, King Ragnald the Cunning, ruler of the Empire, summoned his mages for consult.  Wyrdstone, the precious pieces of the comet which destroyed the once proud city, were finding their way throughout the known world, bringing power, and decay, to all who possessed them.  If King Ragnald could gather a large number of the shards quickly, he knew he could expand the Empire, conquering all that stood in his way, before the ill effects of the stone could affect him.  His plan, retake the city.  But what to do with the many warbands roaming the streets in search of riches and glory?

His plan finally came together.  First, gain a monopoly on the stones.  Next, use the power to pit the warbands against each other while choking off their supplies.  Finally, when the warbands are weak, remove them and take the city.  And that is what he did.  In the end, the warbands were gathered and forced to fight to the death at the amusement of the Empire citizenry.

Ten years have passed since then, and the Empire is thriving.  It has conquered much of the free world and attained riches beyond belief.  The markets are full, and the people (at least those that matter) are fed, and all is good.  However, Mordheim still sits empty.  Too poisonous for anyone to live in permanently.  The wizards continue to harvest wyrdstone, and a large contingent of Empire guards keep out the treasure seekers.  But being a guard is tough, as most die young from the foul influence of the cursed city.  Desertions are common, and the Empire is complacent.  The time is right for the revenge of the warbands.  This time, it is more than just treasure they seek, it is control of the entire abandoned city, and the destruction of the Empire.

The Campaign:

The new campaign will be based on taking control of the city of Mordheim.  Each scenario will represent a sector of the city.  Winners will control the sectors, and gain rewards accordingly.

The attached map shows the sectors within the city, and the order in which scenarios occur.  Winning the scenario means a warband has control of that sector.

Starting a warband:  Due to the shortened nature of the campaign (10 regular play scenarios), warbands will start enhanced.

Each warband will start with 700 gc instead of the normal 500 gc.

Each warband will receive 4 extra wounds to divide among heroes as the player sees fit.  However, no hero may get more than one wound plus up.  When a hero takes a wound plus up at the beginning of the campaign, increase their experience until the next “square” is attained.  The wound counts as the plus up gained for the extra experience.  This extra experience will impact the warbands rating.

Players may purchase +1 WS, +1 BS, +1 I, or +1 Ld for a hero at a cost of 15 gc.  Additional purchases for the same hero will cost 30 gc.  Purchases cannot exceed racial maximums.  No hero may purchase each plus up more than once.  This opportunity only applies to starting warbands.  New heroes hired later in the campaign cannot take advantage.  For the Chaos Marauder character “condemned”, purchasing a plus up counts as if it had been earned during the campaign.  For each plus up a hero purchases, increase their experience until the next “square” is attained.  The chosen plus up counts as the plus up gained for the extra experience.  This extra experience will impact the warbands rating.

That’s one talented lad:  Each warband will have one opportunity during the campaign to declare a henchman plus up as a “The Lad’s Got Talent” result.  The opportunity must be taken before the actual plus up roll is made.

Deserters:  Starting with the second scenario, warbands will find deserters upon entering Mordheim.  Deserters will help the warband during the scenario in return for safe passage out of Mordheim.  Deserters will be Type 1 mercenaries during games 1-5 and Type 2 mercenaries during games 6-10, will increase the warband size for the scenario, but do not count against route when taken out of action.  When the warband routes, deserters will route with them.  No hero may gain more than +2 experience per scenario for taking deserters out of action.

Warbands will get deserters for each scenario based on the warbands overall ranking in the campaign, and the number of sectors the warband controls.  Players ranked 1-2 will receive 1 deserter, 3-4 will receive 2 deserters, 5-6 will receive 3 deserters, and 7-8 will receive 4 deserters.  In addition, before each scenario, players roll a d6 for each sector of Mordheim they control (won the scenario in that sector).  During games 2-6, on a roll of 5-6, they receive an additional deserter.  For games 7-10, they will receive an additional deserter for each roll of 6.

Sector Rewards: Having won a sector will add benefits to a warband during each scenario after action.  After each scenario, for each sector a warband controls (won), consult below and roll a d6 to see what happens.

Scenarios 1, 6 and 10:  Better markets.  On a roll of 5-6, move one column to the right (as if lower ranked) when selling wyrdstone shards.  No warband may move more than one position after each scenario.

Scenarios 2, 7, 8 and 9:  Better haggle.  On a roll of 4-6, you earn the right to add +1 to any one rarity roll during this after action.  Player does not have to declare the plus up until after the roll is made, and no single roll may be increased by more than +1.

Scenarios 3, 4 and 5:  Better recruiting.  On a roll of 5-6, the player may recruit a new henchman into an existing henchman group without worrying about experience available.  When the player exercises this option, the additional experience only costs 1 gc per experience point.

Alternate route rules:  For this campaign, when a warband fails its first route check, the player may choose to try and stay in the fight.  All deserters, well, desert.  Each model from the warband takes a leadership test against their own leadership.  Heroes at -1 Ld, henchmen and hired swords at -2 Ld.  Those that fail leave the playing field.  The player can then choose if those that pass stay or run.  If they choose to stay, all subsequent route checks are at -4 Ld.  When a warband fails its second route check, all models must leave the playing field.

Drugs, Herbs, and Poisons, Oh My:  Healing Herbs, Tears of Shalayla, and Mandrake Root will not be available during this campaign.  All other drugs, herbs, and poisons will be available throughout the campaign, and can be used during any scenario including the finals.  Remember, no model may use more than one drug at a time, and each weapon may only be coated in a single poison at any time.

Finals:  For the finals, all warbands will receive one dose each of Black Lotus, Dark Venom, Madcap Mushrooms, and Crimson Shade.  Additional doses purchased or found during the campaign can be used during the finals.  During the finals, Crimson Shade will only increase a model’s initiative by +1, instead of +d3.

Rank Based Bonuses:  Bonuses are given to each warband after a scenario based on the warbands ranking going into the scenario.  There are two bonuses:  experience and injury re-rolls.  These bonuses are only available after scenarios 5-10.

Experience bonus:  Each warband will get extra hero experience. This experience must be distributed equally among the warbands heroes.  That is, no hero can get a second bonus experience until all heroes have received a first bonus experience.  Warbands ranked 1-4 will receive 1 extra experience.  Warbands ranked 5-6 will receive 3 extra experience.  Warbands ranked 7-8 will receive 5 extra experience.

Injury re-roll bonus:  Players ranked 5 and 6 will receive 1 injury re-roll bonus.  Players ranked 7 and 8 will receive 2 injury re-roll bonuses.  Injury re-rolls can only be used on heroes, and do not carry over between scenarios.  The player can wait until all heroes have completed their regular injury rolls before deciding which models will use the bonus re-rolls.  After the re-roll, the player can choose to accept either the original roll, or the re-roll.  In the case of players ranked 7 and 8, a single model can benefit from both re-rolls.  In that case, the player can choose to accept any one of the three rolls.

Lost the last scenario:  If a warband lost the previous scenario, they may pick a “Favor of the Gods” card at random before the next scenario.  The color of card picked will depend on the warbands rank.  Players ranked 1-3 will pick from the blue cards, 4-6 from the green cards, and 7-8 from the red cards.

MORDHEIM CAMPAIGN HOUSE RULES(as of 19 August 2026):

Campaign Victory Conditions:

At the end of the campaign period, players will be ranked according to their total Win-Loss record, current Warband Rating, and total opponent models taken out of action. These three separate rankings will be added together in a 60/10/30% grouping respectively. The goal is at least 10 rounds of play followed by the finals.  The finals will be a last man standing fight to declare the campaign winner.

Guidelines for arranging Fights and issuing Challenges:

We will play two tables this campaign.

The campaign will include up to 8 players.  Normally, two four player games.  For any table that has only 3 players, one will receive mercenaries based on their opponents rating.  If a table has 2 players, both will receive mercenaries based on their opponents rating.  All table assignments for each round will be determined before the campaign starts.  Each round, the players at each table will roll a d6 and teams will consist of the two highest versus the lowest roll.  For purposes of extra experience gained, players will compare their own rating towards the average of their opponent’s ratings.  If an opponent is teamed with mercenaries, then just compare to the opponent’s rating.

Teams will have the benefit of counting the other warband as friendly models.  Warbands on a team conduct their turns simultaneously.  Friendly models cannot be shot, do not count when determining if a model can run, and may fight together against a single model.  However, spells/prayers may not be cast on the friendly models of another warband, nor do spells/prayers which affect an area of friendly models only have any impact on the other warband of a team.  Warbands use their own leaders for leadership tests, when appropriate, and if one warband on a team routes, the other may still remain in the fight.  Warbands win or lose scenarios as a team.  If one warband meets the scenario criteria for victory, or causes all enemy warbands to route, then all warbands of its team receive a win.

If a warband is fighting alone against an enemy team, then it may receive mercenary help.  To see if a warband receives this help, subtracts its rating from the sum of the ratings of the other two teams.  Divide the remainder by 20 and round up, with a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 12.  That is the number of mercenaries the warband receives.  These mercenaries are their own warband.  As such, they do not count towards the gaining warbands rating, nor do they count for purposes of routing.  These models pass all alone tests.  Once the warband routes, including the turn it routes, mercenaries check for route with a leadership of 7.  If the sum of the ratings of the other two warbands is greater than 400, then use Type 2 mercenaries, otherwise, use Type 1 mercenaries.  Also, the first five mercenaries in a group will count as heroes and come with 2 wounds.

In the case of a two player game, both warbands will receive mercenaries based on the rating of their opponent.  In this case, if the opponent warband’s rating is greater than 250, then the mercenaries are Type 2.

Type 1 Mercenary:  M4 WS4 BS3 S3 T3 W1 I3 A1 Ld8  Sword, Buckler, Dagger

Type 2 Mercenary:  M4 WS5 BS3 S4 T3 W1 I4 A2 Ld8  Sword, Buckler, Toughened Leathers, Dagger  - Expert Swordsman

For post-battle rolls, your opponent MUST witness them. If circumstance prevents this, a neutral witness must be found. Un-witnessed rolls will be overturned, with liberal punitive measures added on, depending on Burgomeister Judgement.

Missing a Night or Starting Over:

If a player misses a night of gaming, then their warband will receive the following to remain competitive in the campaign.  Each hero, hired sword, and henchmen group that can gain experience will receive the base experience for participating in the scenario (usually +1 exp but some scenarios may provide more).  In addition, the warband will receive 30gc.

'Bad luck' may lead your warband to dire circumstance. At any time, you may retire your warband, and start a new one. The new warband may be ANY from the accepted list, and will be created following the campaign rules for starting a warband. You, the Player, will retain your Win-Loss record from warband to warband, but the Rating starts over with each new warband.

There may be times when the “Bad Luck” is such that a player wants to reset its statistics to where it started an evening.  This can only be done with concurrence of the Burgomeister and if one of the following conditions are met:  1) the warband captain suffers a serious injury which does not result in a full recovery or beneficial recovery; 2) the warband has 2 or more heroes that suffer a serious injury which does not result in a full recovery or beneficial recovery; or 3) the warband has 4 or more models which die or suffer serious injuries which do not result in a full recovery or beneficial recovery.  If a warband resets at the end of a night of gaming, after the reset, and to keep the warband competitive in the campaign, each hero, hired sword, and henchmen group that can gain experience will receive the base experience for participating in the scenario (usually +1 exp but some scenarios may provide more).  However, if this plus of experience produces a plus up, and the same plus up was rolled for before the decision to reset was made, then the original plus up will remain with the reset warband.  In addition, the warband will receive 40gc.

Will any 'unofficial' Warbands be allowed?

Generally, NO! See below...

Scenarios

Scenarios will be chosen by the Burgomeister before each fight, and all matches will play the same scenario.  Scenarios are designed to match the campaign theme.

Blood Chits

Every time a hero takes an enemy out of action, he receives a blood chit (keep track of them on the roster sheet).  Blood chits can be cashed in for multiple purposes.

Injuries – after a model rolls for an injury, the player may choose to cash in 7 blood chits to roll again.  If the same result occurs, roll again until a new result occurs.  Pick one of the two results.

Experience plus ups – after a model rolls for an experience plus up, the player may choose to cash in 5 blood chits to roll again.   If the same result occurs, roll again until a new result occurs.  Pick one of the two results.

After the last game of regular play (before finals) any model with 7 or more blood chits remaining may cash them in for a single skill plus up.  If the skill chosen is a spell, a roll for which spell must still be made.

Spells and Abilities which auto Knocked Down, Stun, or Injure

If such spells or abilities are used on a model with multiple wounds left, then successful casting of the spell or use of the skill will cause an automatic wound (no armour saves, regeneration, or other avoidance possible).

Carts & Carnival of Chaos

Placing Models

At the start of a scenario, whenever a warband enters from a table edge (including 8” from the table edge), unless stated otherwise, all it’s models must start on the ground level.  Also, when two warbands make a team, they will both start on the same table edge.  However, they will each start on their own half of that table edge.

Order of Combat

As per the rules, order of combat is determined as follows:  1) take all models that “strike first,” including those that charged.  They fight in order of initiative.  2) Next, take all models that do not strike last, and they fight in order of initiative.  3) Finally, take all models that strike last (due to weapon, standing up, etc), and they fight in order of initiative.  During any block, if multiple models have the same initiative, roll a d6 to determine their order.

Narrow Ledges

The rules state that whenever a model is knocked down/stunned within 1” of a ledge, they must pass an initiative test or fall off the ledge.  For these rolls, a roll of 1 is always a pass, and a roll of 6 is always a fail.  If, however, a model is on a ledge which is narrower than the models base (or on a rope ladder or rope bridge), then the initiative test will be made at +2 to the die roll. This will stack with any other modifiers. A natural roll of 1 will still always pass, and a natural roll of 6 will still always fail.

Fighting over low walls, through windows

The rules state that if a model is up against a low wall (1” high or less) or a window, then an enemy model may charge up to the other side of the wall and be considered in base contact for close combat.  We are modifying the rule slightly.  Now, if a model is within ¼” of a low wall or window, then an enemy model may charge up to the wall and still engage the model in close combat.

Shooting from Windows/Doorways/Ledges

There have been questions to the field of view from windows, doorways, or when standing next to a ledge/low wall.  During a player’s turn, unless stated otherwise, models in these situations will be treated just like any other terrain/cover for purposes of field of view (that is, they can see another model if a line can be drawn from their head to a part of the other model’s body).  However, if behind a window, doorway, or near a ledge, you may declare a model as “leaning out” any time during your turn.  A “leaning out” model gains a 180 degree field of view both in horizontal and vertical (that is, if you can draw a line from the window/doorway, or over the ledge they are standing against to a target), they can see the target.  This also means that until the players next turn, all enemies that can see the window/doorway or appropriate portion of the ledge can also see them.  In addition, any model which is “leaning out” and becomes knocked down/stunned by shooting or a spell must pass an initiative test or fall out the window/doorway or over the ledge.  A model declared “leaning out” is considered to be “leaning out” until the players next turn, at which time the model may again be declared “leaning out” to gain field of view.

Fighting with Two Weapons

We will no longer add a penalty for fighting with two weapons.  All models that can use weapons may now use a weapon in the off-hand with no “to hit” penalty.

Dramatis Personae

Again note, for this campaign no dramatis personae will be available for hire.

Returning the Favor

During exploration, the result of triple 6’s (666) produces a free hired sword.  This seems unbalancing for such a low roll, and it does not treat all warbands fairly.  To adjust this, instead of a free hired sword from the list, the roller will earn two free wardogs (available to any warband which makes the roll, and can be represented with any creature models – chaos hounds, cold ones, etc – but have the wardog stats) that count as hired swords.  These dogs have the stats listed in the equipment portion of the rule book, do NOT count towards the maximum number of warband members, do NOT count as equipment, and do not gain experience.  They increase a warband’s rating by 7 points each, and have an upkeep cost of 5 gc each if you want to keep them after the first fight.  Also, if the dogs are “taken out of action,” they die on a d6 roll of 1-3.

Frenzy

Frenzy compels a model to charge an enemy if they are within range.  The official interpretation says any model within charge range (even if there is no line of sight) can be considered a potential target.  These house rules will modify that interpretation.  If a model which has frenzy does not charge during the normal charge phase, then at the end of the phase check to see if there are any models it must charge.  Any model within charge range with a clear line of sight is a potential target.  For any model within 4” of the frenzied model for which there is no clear line of sight, perform an initiative test.  If the test is passed, the model is also a potential target.  Once all of the potential targets have been identified, the model may choose one of them to charge.

Nobody is Invincible

No warrior should be invincible.  In close combat only, any model with a base 3 strength or higher will always wound an enemy model on a “to wound” roll of 6, even if the combat tables state that a wound is not possible. In the case that the combat tables show a wound is not possible, the roll of 6 will never cause a critical hit, and the enemy model will always get an armour save at +2.  If the model has no armour, it will get a 5+ armour save.

Spells

When forming a warband before the first scenario, hero spellcasters will start with a spell of their choice from those available to the warband.  When hiring warband heroes with spells later in the campaign, first roll two dice (re-rolling one die if doubles are rolled) and choose one for the starting spell.  You may choose not to hire the hero if you do not like either spell, but must wait until after the next scenario to try again.  When heroes choose a new spell instead of a skill, again roll two dice (re-rolling one die if doubles are rolled) and choose one as the plus-up.

For hired swords, you may roll for their spells, as normal, before deciding to hire them.  However, if you choose not to hire them, you must wait until after the next scenario to try again.

Line of Sight (LOS)

For charging, shooting and casting spells, the following definitions of LOS will be used.

Terrain:  Terrain is fixed and offers well defined cover.  In order to have a LOS on a miniature behind terrain, you must be able to draw a line from the head of the viewer to a visible body part of the target.

Other miniatures:  Other miniatures are considered to be moving and just occupying an area represented by the miniature.  Therefore, other miniatures provide cover for shooting but do not block a LOS.

Charging:

There have been questions on the sequence for charging.  This is house interpretation of the charging rules:

First, declare all charges.  You must have a LOS to the target unless an initiative test is passed as per the rules in the rule book.  All declared charges must have a clear, base wide path to the target.  Declare charges regardless of whether the opponent can intercept them.  Note you can see through close combat to find a charge target.

Next, in any order the charging player desires, measure the charge distance for each charge.  If the model is in charge distance, then prepare to move it to the target.  If there are any unengaged enemy models within ~2 inches of the charge path they may attempt to intercept the charge.  If a model wants to intercept, see the “Interception Defined” section below.  Note that only one model may attempt to intercept any charge.  If the charger causes fear and the interceptor fails a leadership test, then no models may intercept that particular charger.

Note, intercepting models, or models which have charged earlier in the sequence could make a later charge invalid due to blocked paths, etc.  In this case, a model cut off from its intended target will suffer a failed charge.

Reasonable Charge:  If a player attempts what should be considered an unreasonable charge (ex:  across the board) to avoid a compulsory move, it may be challenged by the other players.  If it is challenged, have all players involved turn their backs to the table, and have a neutral player measure the charge distance.  If the distance is greater than 1.5 times the model’s charge range, declare the charge unreasonable.  The charge is then considered void (not failed) and the player can use the model as normal.

Charging multiple opponents and interception

When a model chooses to charge multiple enemies, the standard rules only allow a model not involved in the charge to intercept.  This new house rule will allow one of the multiple models charged to intercept under certain conditions.  When a model declares a charge on multiple enemies, plot the most direct charge route to leave the charger in base contact with both models.  Now plot the same route but ending in base contact with just one model at a time (shortest distance to base contact).   If the route to any one model is at least 1” shorter than the route to multiple models, then that model may choose to intercept.  Only one model can intercept any charge.

Interception defined

After a warband/team has declared all of its charges, the charging models are moved one at a time.  When a player begins the actual movement of a charging model, a single enemy model may be declared as an interceptor.  If a player declares a model as an interceptor, proceed in the following manner.  First, move the charging model the first 2” (or less if closer) along the charge path along the shortest route to the charged model.  Next, check to see if the intercepting model can intercept.  If the intercepting model has a clear (base wide) path no greater than 2" in length that places any part of the intercepting model’s base on the center of the charge path (the line representing the shortest path from the charger to the charged model) somewhere between the charging model's current location (after the 2" movement) and the charged model's location, then the intercept is successful.  Move the intercepting model to the intercept location and move the charging model along the charge path into base contact with the interceptor.  If, however, the intercepting model cannot reach the charge path between the charger and the charged model as described above, then the intercept fails.  A model which fails an intercept cannot attempt to intercept any other models during that movement phase.

Shooting through combat or friendly players

The rules specifically state that you cannot shoot into close combat.  You will be allowed to shoot through close combat and/or friendly models at a suitable target.  However, if you do, keep in mind the shooting rule on page 14 of the living rulebook.  The target receives cover from the models in close combat/friendlies.  We no longer will allow shots to hit the cover.  Also, friendly models in base contact that are along the line of sight for a shot will provide cover.

Multiple Shots or Attacks

Models with multiple missile weapon shots in a single turn must declare all shots before rolling to hit.  Likewise, models with multiple close combat attacks must declare all attacks before rolling to hit.  The one exception is the Saurus bite attack which occurs after all other attacks.  Its target may be declared when it happens.

Silver Arrows of Ahra

There is concern that the Lesser Magic spell Silver Arrows of Ahra is too powerful.  When successfully cast, we will reduce the number of arrows to d6+1.  The arrows will still be capable of causing critical wounds.

Elevated models and shooting

With the addition of multiple planks between buildings on the upper levels, we have reduced the benefit of elevated shooting.  Models in elevated positions will only treat models 1 plank away as a threat for determining targets.  If models are on the same level as the shooter, but would have to cross 2 or more planks to reach the shooter, the shooter may ignore them and choose its target instead.

Crawling from close combat

Note:  As per page 17 of the living rulebook, “If he is in base-to-base contact with an enemy, a knocked down model may crawl 2” away only if the enemy is engaged in hand-to-hand combat with another opponent, otherwise he has to stay where he is.”

Spear rules

Under the current rules, when receiving a charge, a model armed with a spear benefits from “first strike.”  For this campaign, along with the benefit of “first strike,” a spear armed model receiving a charge fights at +1 Initiative against the charger.  Note:  A model equipped with a spear may only use a buckler or a shield in the other hand.

Orc Spell Led’z Go

The orc spell Led’z Go gives models strike first, regardless of other circumstances.  That means models that stood up, or are using a double-handed weapon and usually would strike last now “strike first.”  Remember, multiple models may have “strike first” from charging, spear, or other methods.  If more than one model in a close combat has “strike first” they are still resolved in order of initiative before all models without “strike first.”

Lance rules

The lance will be treated just like a spear with “first strike” with +1 Initiative when receiving a charge, and a “Cavalry Bonus” of +2 Strength on a charge (no additional +2 Strength all the time).  Lances can only be used when mounted, and can only be combined with a shield or buckler.

Nets

Nets take the place of bucklers and shields in a model’s equipment list.  If used in combat, a net can be used to parry an attack.  Just like other parry equipment, it must be used to parry the highest hit roll in the first round of attacks that scores a hit.  If the net successfully parries an attack, it parries all attacks from that weapon for that round.

Armour

Anyone wearing Ithilmar, Gromril, or Chaos Armour can force the Re-roll of any Critical Hit Chart Results against them, but if re-rolled, they must accept the second roll.

Shields and bucklers will now add an additional +1 to an armour save (+1 for bucklers and +2 total for shields) in close combat only (not against missile fire).

An additional benefit to equipping with armour will occur during serious injuries roles.  After a fight, any model required to make a serious injury role (whether hero, henchman or hired sword/dramatis personae) can first make a base armour save (no strength modifiers, no additional plus for shields or bucklers).  Also, if a model is wearing a helmet, they get an additional +1 to this save role.  Note, if a model has a natural armour save of any kind (thick skin, shaggy hide, etc), then the use of a helmet will not offer a bonus for this role.  If passed, treat the injury as a “full recovery,” otherwise role on the serious injury chart as normal.  Barding will not count towards a person’s base save, although the +1 bonus from the mount will.  Even if this armour save is passed, the model counts as having been taken out of action for purposes of exploration and searching the market for rare items.

Amulets of life

Amulets of Life may be purchased as equipment.  Once purchased, amulets are considered heirlooms and cannot be sold.  These amulets provide no benefit during the scenario except for in the after action phase.  Amulets provide a save versus serious injury just like armour above.  They do not stack with other amulets, or armour, but may be used instead of the armour worn by the model.  There are types of amulet, those for heroes only, and those for any model.  Hero only versions are common, and come in 6+ save for 10gc, 5+ save for 20gc, and 4+ save for 40gc.  The all versions can be equipped by heroes and henchmen (including animals, but no hired swords) but have rarity.  The all versions come in 6+ save for 15gc and rarity 6, 5+ save for 25gc and rarity 7, and 4+ save for 45gc and rarity 8.

Multiple Drugs or Poisons

Models may only use one form of drug at any time.  Additional drugs taken for a scenario will have no effect.  Drugs can raise a characteristic above the racial maximum.  Likewise, a weapon may only be coated with one type of poison for each scenario.

Nurgle’s Rot

In the Carnival of Chaos warband, the heroes called Tainted Ones can begin with Nurgle’s Rot.  While not specifically stated, we will assume that the Carnival of Chaos warband, due to their already plague and disease ridden bodies, are immune to its effects.

Once a member of another warband has contracted the disease, the player will role before each battle to see if it is spread within the warband.  On a roll of 6, another member of the warband will contract the rot and suffer the effects as normal.  Randomly roll, if the chosen player is immune to disease then it does not spread.  Members of other warbands which contract the rot will also obtain the ability to transfer it to an opponent in hand-to-hand combat by rolling a 6 when hitting.

Trolls, while not immune to disease, have a special resistance to the rot due to their regenerative powers.  A troll that has the rot, makes its toughness test at +1T (a good thing here).  Also, if the player rolls a natural 1, then the troll may regain 1 toughness previously lost to the disease.  However, a troll which has its toughness reduced to zero is lost permanently from the game.

Finally, a cure for the rot does exist.  The Madcap Shade tea is very potent, and sometimes has adverse effects.  It has a rarity of 8, costs 20+2d6 gc, and cures the disease on a 4+.  If the model rolls a 6 when drinking the tea, his toughness is increased by 1, up to racial maximum.  However, if a 1 is rolled, then not only does the tea fail, but the model loses 1 toughness.

Climb Up and Down, Climb and Charge:

Models will not be able to “run” up walls, unless they have the Scale Sheer Surfaces skill.  Models may run to the wall, and then climb as long as they have sufficient non-running movement left.

When descending, models may have the option of jumping or climbing down a wall.  The rules treat both the same in risk of injury, however climbing down costs movement while jumping down does not.  From now on, if a model jumps down, it is at normal initiative.  If a model climbs down, and thus uses movement, it will be accomplished at +1I.

You can Climb and then charge an opponent at the top. Simply double your move, subtract the climb distance (regular movement not doubled), and use the rest to charge.

For this campaign, models need not start in contact with a wall to climb it in the same turn. Charges are still limited by LOS to target or spotting range. Initiative Tests are still required to climb.

scenarios.name: The Poor Quarter Thieves Hideout
scenarios.narrative: The warbands first push back into Mordheim occurs in the Poor Quarter.  While the warbands expect to find little of value in this part of Mordheim, there is one glimmer of hope.  It was fabled that a gang of street urchin thieves hid in an orphanage in the Poor Quarter, and maybe they left something of value behind.  As your warbands converge on the old orphanage building, they realize a group of Empire guards are inside searching for treasure of their own.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain

Place a multi-story building at the center of the table to represent the orphanage.  Fill in the rest of the play area with additional terrain pieces.  However, no additional terrain pieces may be placed within 4” of the center building.
scenarios.deployment:
Warband Setup

Each player rolls a dice. Whoever rolls highest chooses who sets up first. The first player then chooses which table edge to set up on, placing all his warriors within 4" of that edge. His opponent then sets up within 4" of the opposite edge.

Starting the game

Both players roll a D6. The higher scoring player takes the first turn.
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

Empire Guards

Place five Empire Guards in the center building, three on the ground floor, and two on the second floor.  The guards will be a third team in the scenario, and their turn is last in the sequence.  The guards stats and gear are as follows:

M4 WS3 BS3 S3 T3 W1 I3 A1 Ld7

Halberd, Bow, Light Armor, Helmet

The guards will never leave the center building.  If there are enemy models within the center building that they can see, they will charge the nearest model.  However, they will never charge a fear causing model.  If the closest model is fear causing and there are non-fear causing model they can charge, the guards will charge the closest non-fear causing model.  If not engaged in close combat, the guards will attempt to shoot the closest enemy model.

Searching the Thieves Hideout

Any hero that ends their turn standing within the center building, and without having shot, cast a spell, or participated in close combat during that turn, may search the Thieves Hideout for hidden treasure.  In doing so, the hero receives a search token which may be used during the scenario after action. Search tokens are never lost, even if the model is taken out of action or its warband routes.
scenarios.victory:
Ending the game

When all but one of the warbands routes, the game ends.

Winning the game

The game is won by causing all enemy warbands to route.  When a team wins, all heroes on the winning team that were not taken out of action during the scenario earn two additional search tokens for the Thieves Hideout.
scenarios.experience:
Experience

+1 Survives. If a Hero or a Henchman group survives the battle they gain +1 Experience.

+1 Winning Leader. The leader of the winning warband gains +1 extra Experience.

+1 Per Enemy Out of Action. Any Hero earns +1 Experience for each enemy model he puts out of action, including Empire guards.

+1 for Empire guards Out of Action.  Any henchmen group or hired sword that takes an Empire guard out of action earns +1 experience.  No henchmen group or hired sword may gain more than +1 experience this way.
scenarios.rewards:
The Spoils

Normal searching for wyrdstone occurs after this scenario.  In addition:

The Empire guards had found a Master Mordheim Map in the Theives Hideout.  Due to its value, they had no intention of leaving it behind.  If the scenario ends with any Empire guards not taken out of action, then the guards escape with the map during the chaos of the fight ending.  Otherwise, every warband on the winning team receives a Master Mordheim Map which allows the re-roll of any one die during each exploration.

Also, each hero gets to roll a d6 for each search token they received.  For each die that comes up 5-6, the hero found something of importance in the Thieves Hideout.  Roll an additional d6, if a 6 is rolled, the hero has found a Ring of +1 Initiative.  Otherwise, each “important” find is worth 5 gc to the warband.  No warband may find more than one Ring of +1 Initiative.

scenarios.name: The Bridge
scenarios.narrative: Having lost control of the entertainment district, Empire forces have pulled back to the other side of the river.  In the chaos of the retreat the empire troops dropped some wyrdstone before and after crossing the bridge.  Scouting parties returning from the far side have discovered the wyrdstone but the rest of the warband remains spread out on the far side of the river.  With other warbands arriving on scene, only quick reinforcement will ensure the prize is won.  This scenario plays as a modified version of the Wyrdstone Hunt scenario.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain

Setup up terrain as normal but mark out a 3” river as shown in the figure below (river is slightly offset to the top side such that the bottom river bank is 24” from the table edge) and place a bridge crossing the river in the center.  Define the direction of flow as shown.  Place four markers for wyrdstone on the far side of the bridge and two markers on the near side relative to the deployment zones.  Place the markers within ~4-6” of the bridge, roughly as shown below.  These markers represent wyrdstone lost by the retreating troops.  The area within 2” of the river is the riverbank.
scenarios.deployment:
Setup

Roll for teams as normal but instead of rolling to determine sides and turn order, roll to determine who chooses between two options: pick starting zone, setup second and go second or let the other side pick the side and then setup and go first.  The teams will setup in the deployment zones shown on the figure above (12x8” from the corner).
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

The River

The river running through Mordheim is polluted and difficult to cross.  Any model may cross the river but will be at half movement in the water even if they have the aquatic ability since the river is so treacherous.  Note that models cannot “run” while swimming across the river.  Models in heavy armor can cross the river but do so at ¼ movement, though dwarves and models on horseback are exempt from this rule.  Any model that is forced off of the board is immediately taken out of action and any wyrdstone they are carrying is lost, but will only roll for injuries after the game on a roll of 1-2 on a D6.  Any model that is knocked down or stunned in the river will need to take a strength test in the recovery phase to recover (otherwise they remain knocked down or stunned), though a model that recovers from knocked down will not suffer additional movement penalties (i.e. the ½ movement penalty for recovery does not stack with the river penalty).  Any model that spends any portion of their movement phase in the river will be swept downstream D6”.  Resolve the downstream movement at the end of the model’s movement phase or prior to exiting the river whichever occurs first.  Note that models with the aquatic ability roll D3” instead of D6” for downstream movement.  The river bank is steeply sloped and challenging to cross and will be considered difficult terrain (1/2 movement but model can run) unless a model passes an initiative test when headed into the river and a strength test when getting out of the river.  Any model that begins and ends its turn on the same river bank slips and falls back into the river.  Immediately have them swept downriver d6" and place them at the center of the river.

Models cannot fight in the river or on the river banks.  Models in the river cannot declare charges (swimming isn’t conducive to charging).  Models in the river count as having cover, and only models within 12” of the river can shoot at a model in the river due to the steep banks.  For the purposes of determining when a model is in the river/on the river bank, use the halfway point of the model’s base as the delineation, i.e. a model is only considered on the river bank or in the river if half or more of their base falls in the area.

Wyrdstone

Any non-animal model can pick up a wyrdstone by ending their movement at the marker.  Models can only carry one wyrdstone and cannot pass it off to another model.  If a model carrying a wyrdstone is knocked down, stunned or taken out of action, the wydstone is dropped and scatters D3” in a random direction.  When a warband routes roll D6 for every wyrdstone carried by a model on the far side of the river on a roll of 1-2 the wyrdstone is lost as the warband member tries to flee back across the river.  As with other scenarios any wyrdstone collected by one member of the team is credited to both warbands.  Warbands add +1 to their leadership for route checks for each wyrdstone their warband holds (max +2), wyrdstone held by a teammate does not count.
scenarios.victory:
Ending the game

The game ends when one team completely routes or when one of the teams successfully moves 3 or more wyrdstone off of the board.  Models can only exit the board on the edge between the two deployment zones (i.e. the bottom edge on the figure above).  Warbands automatically keep any wyrdstone that is successfully moved off the board, but they no longer get the leadership bonus for that wyrdstone.
scenarios.experience:
Experience

+1 Survives. If a Hero or a Henchman group survives the battle they gain +1 Experience.

+1 Winning Leader. The leader of the winning warband gains +1 extra Experience.

+1 Per Enemy Out of Action. Any Hero earns +1 Experience for each enemy model he puts out of action.  They earn an extra +1 XP (max 3 extra) if they were holding a wyrdstone when they take out an enemy model.

+1 Wyrdstone. Any model that leaves the board or finishes the game with a wyrdstone earns +1 XP.
scenarios.rewards: Apply the collected Wyrdstone and scenario-specific rewards described in the special rules; resolve these manually.

scenarios.name: Executioner’s Square
scenarios.narrative: Throughout the past decade, numerous small warbands and individuals have been caught by Empire troops trying to enter or leave Mordheim.  These unlucky adventurers ended up in prisons within the city, often used as slave labor to retrieve wyrdstone from the more unsavory parts of the city.  With the Empire forces in disarray and the warbands advancing, the decision has been made to liquidate the few remaining prisoners.  The prison guards decide it is fitting to take the prisoners to the Executioner’s Square to perform one last task before their demise.  The square has been haunted ever since it was the scene of a large massacre of warbands deemed too weak to fight in the Empire’s celebratory games.  The warbands’ weapons, armor, equipment and money had been piled up to be retrieved later, but those sent to retrieve the items returned stark raving mad, gibbering about the terrible things inhabiting the square.  Ever since no one has dared to enter the square, but the guards send the prisoners into the square with their hands bound and their feet hobbled to retrieve the loot, promising release to those who return with loot and swift death to those who don’t.  The arrival of the warbands has scared off the guards but the lure of the loot remains...  This scenario plays as a modified version of the “King of the Mountain” scenario.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain

Setup up terrain as normal, but leave a large opening in the center of the board to represent the Executioner’s Square at least 12”x12”.  Place a small statue, fountain or other small terrain piece to mark the center of square where the armor, weapons and gold is piled up.
scenarios.deployment:
Warbands

Each team rolls a die. Whoever rolls highest chooses who sets up first. The first team then chooses which sides to set up on, placing all his warriors within the 8” of that edge.  His opponent then sets up within 8” of the opposite edge.
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

Prisoners

Each player will need two extra models to represent the prisoners (not models already in the warband).  The prisoners are henchmen models from the warband type of each player.  The models are selected from the two most commonly available henchmen (i.e. pick the two types with the highest number of allowable models).  For example, for lizardmen place an extra Saurus and Skink on the table to be prisoners.  Only select models that can gain experience and never select large models (if necessary select two of the same henchman type).  If two henchmen groups have the same limit, player may decide which to use.  After both sides have setup, place these models in the square D3+1” in a D8 direction from the center.  During each team’s movement phase each player can move those prisoners that belong to their warband.  The prisoner’s move at half movement and cannot run, charge or fight back if charged (attacker is at +1 to hit a bound prisoner).  Any prisoner that starts their movement next to a friendly model will have their bonds cut if both models perform no other action during their turn.  After being freed the prisoner will have a dagger and the lowest cost hand weapon they have access to (typically a club/mace/hammer).  If the prisoner can fight with no weapons without penalty then they will just have a dagger.  After this point the prisoner can move and fight as normal using their base stats for shooting and combat.

Claiming the Mountain of Loot

Any warband member may claim the mountain of loot (though bound prisoners cannot), and multiple players, even from both teams, may claim the loot at the same time.  To claim the loot, a character must move within 6” of the table center (the “Ring of Fire”) and declare they are “claiming the mountain.”  While “claiming the mountain,” a character may move, charge, shoot, cast and fight as normal.  However, if the character is knocked down, stunned, or moves more than 6” from the table center (out of the “Ring of Fire”), they have lost their claim and must declare it all over again.  In order to become “King of the Mountain”, a character must have claimed the loot, and also:

1)  started two consecutive turns having claimed the mountain

2)  finished both turns still claiming the mountain

3)  finish both turns with no standing enemy models (including prisoners) within 6” of center

Models outside the “Ring of Fire” may choose to run towards the mountain of loot, even if there are enemy models within 8”.  Models which make this choice must move maximum distance along the shortest route to the loot.  This will be the only action for the model that turn.  Models which choose this action may not shoot, cast spells, or participate in close combat the turn they run.

The Haunting Spirits

The spirits haunting the executioner’s square are very possessive of the loot piled up at the center.  At the end of every round, roll 2D6 to determine what the disturbed spirits of the dead do to those who have dared to threaten their loot.  The ghosts only attack models within 6” of the loot pile.  Note that models immune to psychology are affected by the results below but test at +2 leadership (roll of 12 always fails).  The leadership rule (using the warband leader’s leadership) applies for all required tests, but any warband who takes out a bound prisoner within 6” of the center will test at -2 to their leadership for the next D3 rounds.

2-3, Ghost attack: Ghosts attack models threatening the loot (i.e. models within 6” as noted above), D3 models from each warband closest to the center are attacked by ghosts (roll D3 to determine number attacked and then determine the closest models).  Instead of rolling to hit, each model must take a leadership test, if they fail, the model then takes a strength test to see whether the attack “wounds”.  If “wounded” by a ghost the model will break and flee but will not lose wounds (if in combat no free hits are allowed), see rule book for rules on fleeing models. In short: model runs 2D6” toward nearest table edge.  They can recover with a successful leadership test during the recovery phase otherwise they keep running 2D6”, if they reach the table edge they are removed from combat but do not roll for after-action injury.

4-6, Unearthly howl: the spirits let out a piercing shriek that cuts to the heart of every living heart near the loot.  D3 models in each warband closest to the loot must take a leadership test.  If they fail they will be at -1 I and -1 to hit in both shooting and close combat during the next round.

7-9, Ghostly apparitions: Frightening apparitions appear to drive away models getting too close to the loot.  D3 unengaged models from each warband closest to the loot must take a leadership test.  If failed the model will immediately move D6” in a random direction.  When moving the model ignore any obstacles in their way and instead place the model at the specified distance and direction.  If there is another model in that spot or the spot would have the model end up closer to the pile, continuing moving the model in the same direction until a clear spot is available and/or they end up further from the loot pile than they started.

10-12, Haunted whispering: the spirits whisper dark and terrible things to the D3 models from each warband closest to the loot and not engaged in combat.  The models must pass a leadership test.  If they fail, roll a D6 to determine the result.  The results will be in effect for the next round only.

Roll of 1: animosity, the model suffers from animosity, follow normal rules for animosity but model is automatically affected and use following D6 results instead of the normal orc/goblin rules: (1-2: charge nearest unengaged friendly, 3-4: do nothing, 5-6: charge nearest enemy if able)

Roll of 2-3: stupidity, the model rolls for stupidity (i.e. 1-3: shambles forward at half movement, 4-6: do nothing)

Roll of 4-5: blood lust, the model automatically charges the nearest enemy model, or if unable moves as close as possible toward the nearest enemy model

Roll of 6: frenzy, the model must charge an enemy model and doubles the number of attacks they get.

scenarios.name: Heart of the Cemetery
scenarios.narrative:
Your warband had heard that the Empire’s wizards were going to smuggle out a supply of their Wyrdstones to other reaches of The Empire for the ongoing wars. Something however, went terribly wrong. The wagon, while cutting through the cemetery, suddenly exploded leveling various Mausoleums nearby. Undead have started to rise throughout the graveyard, more so the closer you get to the wagon of wyrdstones. In reality, this was a trap by the wizards trying to wipe out several warbands, though the volatility of the wyrdstones as well as the cursed location blew up. Warbands, and guards that arrived, seemed to ignore their usual animosity towards one and other in trying to destroy the mass of undead.

Your warband, and others, are furiously engaged in combat around the Cemetery with a small group heading towards the center to try for the wagon full of Wyrdstone, perhaps if you remove enough the undead will stop rising.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain

Starting area is a 24” diameter Circle, 4 2” wide entry points 90° apart from each other. Center 2” circle is the cart with 8 numbers midway between the center of the board and edge.

No Terrain: The Mausoleums were leveled in the explosion, though oddly the cart remains untouched at the center of the board.
scenarios.deployment:
Wabands

The warbands have a loose alliance, mindless undead pouring out of the cemetery would be bad for all whether it be for concern of the danger, or a rival in one’s own plans. Any Vampire warbands present aid due to detecting some malevolent power that they wish not contend with as their Necromancers have no power over these particular undead. As such, warbands do not count as enemies for the purpose of targets or spells.

All members are considered to be engaged in battle throughout the cemetery, managing to slip in a few warriors to try and make a break for the center wagon periodically

Turn Order:

The cemetery denizens will not start spawning until the round after the first shard is taken

Turns will be randomized each round starting with round they spawn + place on spawn point.
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

Deserters and City Guards:

Starting on the rounds the zombies spawn, a deserter (Based upon base house rules) from each warband may attempt to enter the field.

Roll 1D6, on a 3+ a Deserter enters the heart of the Cemetery reduce the difficulty by 1 for each round until a Deserter is in play for that warband. If there are no deserters left on that warband team a City Guard may come to help, if there are no deserters/city guards on the field for your warband roll 1d6 on a 5+ a city guard will come join you. There may only be 1 deserter/city guard per team on the table at any given time.

Special Rule: City Guards act at +1 Leadership value for the purposes of overcoming the fear of Undead.

Starting the Game

There is a near limitless supply of wyrdstone within the wagon. Any hero, hired sword or Henchman may end their turn at the wagon (whether by charging or moving). Animals, and mindless creatures, may come to the field but may not loot shards.

At the end of their turn, provided they are not engaged in close combat or if all of their opponents are knocked down/stunned they may loot a stone.

Each warband may choose a Hero and Henchman/Hired Sword group to enter the field of battle. They may only leave the field from a gate that was not their entry point. The same hero and/or henchmen group may not return to the table they just left unless they are the only choice left available (this includes Animals)

Once the Undead start spawning, there will be D3+1 (D3 if 3 player game, D2 if 2 player game) Undead every turn.

Max number: <12/9/8> Zombies or Skeletons, <6/5/4> Grave Guard.

These undead appear as the follows:

1 undead in the center of the cart (If there is already 1 at the cart, deploy as per next option

The Rest located around the halfway point (1-8) between the center and the board edge

The Wyrd-Wraith will always appear at the center Cart, even if an undead from a previous round is still there.

The target priority are as follows: (Wyrdwraith always declares/charges first, then closest creatures)

Anyone the Wyrdwraith is attacking alone.

Anyone with a Wyrdstone, who is unengaged.

Any Unengaged model

Anyone with a Wyrdstone

Anyone else provided they are in charge range.

Stay and guard the cart

Once the Wyrd-Wraith appears, there will be no new Grave guard to spawn until the number, including the wraith, becomes less than the scenario max based upon number of players.

Advancing the Phase:

After <10/8/6> shards have been removed from the board, or 1 hour after the start of the Scenario, a burst of energy emanates from the Cart of Wyrdstone. All zombies on the field have their flesh melt away before your eyes transforming them into skeletons.

After <14/11/8> shards have been removed from the board, or 2 hours have passed since the start of the scenario a stronger burst will emanate from the cart, all skeletons crumble to the ground and instantly reform, up to their max number,  as armed Grave Guards (instantly remaining in combat with anyone they previously were engaged with). They return based upon the Max number of Grave Guards, with those in close combat  being returned first, if not enough/others remaining randomize between engaged models first.

After <18/14/10> shards have been removed from the board, or 3.25 hours have passed since the start of the scenario, the Wyrdstones on the cart melt away to near nothing (can still be looted) and a Wyrd-Wraith rises from the cart, intent on killing all life.

The Enemies:

Zombie | 4 | 2 | 0 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 5

Special Rules: Undead (Immune to Psychology & Poison, Cause Fear, No-Pain) Can’t Run, No Brain

Special Rules:

For purposes of Psychology/special abilities the following rules apply:

Running: Other warband models do not count as enemies in this scenario, nor do the City Guards, May run if no unengaged undead within 8”

Frenzy: The cart may be ran to instead of charging a model. If holding a shard they may move at the fastest speed available towards the nearest (and only nearest) exit point for them.

Stupidity: The ‘Shamble forward’ result will either move them towards the Cart, or nearest legal exit depending on if they have a shard or not.

Infiltrate: May not be used in this scenario.

Route Check: There are no route checks made on this scenario

Undead Charges: Undead allied with the Wyrd-Wraith will not need to declare charges, but will instead charge based upon the charge priorities.

Cannot Engage: Any unit may break from combat with the Wraith at any time, he cannot hold engagement while ethereal, though, his undead minions however may hold you in place. The Wraith also does not get the usual automatic hit for breaking from combat.
scenarios.victory:
Ending the Game

The game ends when the Wyrd-wraith is destroyed, players stop bringing units into the heart of the cemetery, or the allotted time is hit. It is assumed, if the Wyrd-Wraith is not destroyed, that the wizards managed to trap it in the heart of the cemetery. If the time limit is hit, the game halts immediately, even mid swing, as the Wyrd-wraith lets out a banshee howl driving all away from the heart. In either of the latter cases, nobody gains control of this district.

If the Wyrd-wraith is killed, all Hero’s and groups keep and get credit for the Wyrdstones they’re holding. If the Wyrd-wraith lets out the Banshee howl, all stones currently in the hands of models are dropped as you flee.

Winning the Game

There will be at Maximum, 1 winner and 1 loser, it is possible for all ties.

To determine who wins, ties, or loses, calculate the below standard.

Henchmen/Hired Sword group kills are maxed out at 5 points per group

Hero kills are maxed at: 4 Zombie/Skeleton, 3 Grave Guard (10 possible points)

Deserter kills are maxed at 1 Zombie/Skeletons, 1 Grave Guard (3 possible points)

Zombies/Skeletons: 1 pt

Grave Guard: 2 pts

DreadWraith: 2 pts per wound done, even if ‘maxed out’ as per above

Wyrdstone: 1 point per stone removed from the board up 8, afterwards, 2 victory points per stone.

In event of a tie for top place, there will be 2 ties (unless one side got the killing blow on the wraith)

Really winning the game: If the Dread Wraith is slain, whoever ‘wins’ the scenario also gains control of the zone and its bonus.

Hero Experience gains: +1 for removing a Wyrdstone from the board (Max 4) , +1 for Killing a Zombie or Skeleton (Max 4xp), +2 for Killing a Grave Guard (Max 4xp), +2xp per wound inflicted on the Wyrd-wraith (Max 4)

Henchmen/Hired Swords: +1xp per Wyrdstone removed from board (Multiple models still only get 1 per sortee into the fray for xp and shards), +1 per wound inflicted on the Wyrd-wraith

There is no searching after this scenario. What you get is what you get from the rewards/Shards.

scenarios.name: The Temple of Morr
scenarios.narrative: The Temple of Morr is now a dark and empty husk, but rumor has it that on a full moon it also forms a gateway to the Netherworld and that hearty warbands can retrieve fallen comrades and gain great rewards from Morr, the God of Death. However, Morr demands a steep price and is quick to punish those who fail to appease him. For this scenario to work, warbands must have kept track of all henchmen (including stats, gear, experience, etc) which have died during previous scenarios.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain

Setup buildings and terrain with a large building in the center that represents the Temple of Morr with open space around it. Also leave open an 8” space on one side of the board to represent the Netherworld.
scenarios.deployment:
Starting the game

Each player rolls a die. Whoever rolls highest chooses to set up first or passes. The first player to set up then chooses which table edge to set up on, placing all his warriors within 8" of that edge. His opponent then sets up within 8" of the opposite edge. Both teams roll a D6. The higher scoring side takes the first turn.
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

The Netherworld

During a full moon, the Temple of Morr and the Netherworld become aligned, and those who please Morr acts of violence can enter his realm and seek rewards from him. To represent this, every TOA a warband has during the game will provide favors, a deserter = 1 favor, a henchman = 2, and a Hero/large model = 3 favors. Keep track of when favors are used as they can only be used once.

Warbands may not enter the Netherworld until after they have caused their first wound against an opponent in the scenario.  Once a wound has been done, at the end of a player’s combat phase, 1 Hero from his/her warband may enter the Netherworld to seek rewards. Any Hero who had a TOA during the preceding round enters for free. Otherwise, the cost to enter depends on the model’s distance from the temple and the total number of successful petitions on the table. Additionally, a cost is levied if a player chooses to face a normal shadow depending on the total number of normal shadows are defeated on the table, as Morr grows bored with easy combat.

Total Successful Petitions  (for 2/3 player game subtract one) | Distance from Temple | Cost to face Normal Shadow
 | <6” | >6” | Total  # of  defeated  Normals | Cost
< 4   | Free | 1 | < 4 | 0
4-5  | 1 | 2 | 4-5 | 1
>5 | 2 | 3 | >5 | 2

Heroes who have successfully petitioned the Netherlord are no longer eligible for further entry. If the player decides to send a Hero, they will remove that Hero from the board and place it in the Netherworld and mark off any favors used. Additional favors are used to aid the Hero in the Netherworld, see below.

The Netherworld

Morr does not give rewards lightly and every model that enters the Netherworld will have to prove themselves worthy of Morr’s patronage. To fairly test the heart of each warrior, Morr creates a shadow of the model who enters his realm and only rewards those who can defeat their shadow. Those seeking the greatest reward can also chose to face a more advanced challenge. Shadows will start with the same stats, weapons, and skills as the player’s model with the following modifications:

Shadows

 | M | WS | BS | S | T | W | I | A | Ld | Wpns /Armor | Special Rules/Skills
Normal |  |  |  |  |  | -1 | -1 |  |  | Same  wpns /No Armor | No  skills  or spells , immune to poison
Advanced |  | +1 |  | +1 |  |  |  |  |  | Same | No  spells , immune to poison

Note: Stats cannot be reduced below one.Note: Stats cannot be reduced below one.The player can use favors to reduce the stats of the shadow based on the costs listed in the table below. The cost is paid for each stat individually and cost increases for each additional reduction of that stat. For example, reducing Initiative and WS by 1 costs two favors, but reducing WS by 2 would cost 3 favors (1 for the first and 2 for the second).

Category | First | Second | Third
Initiative, WS, BS | 1  | 2  | 3
Strength, Wounds | 2  | 3 | 4
Attacks, Toughness  / Skills,  Armor | 2 | 4 | 6

Combat in the underworld immediately follows the end of the combat phase and will proceed as follows:

Player chooses which opponent to face (Normal or Advanced) and spends favors for modifiers

Set the Hero 5” from the model representing the shadow

Turn order is determined randomly by highest roll, but the side with the higher initiative adds the difference in initiative to their roll, (i.e. if I=4 vs. I=3, then I=4 model adds one to die roll)

Play out the combat following normal rules (models may move, shoot, cast spells, charge, etc.)

The shadow model will be controlled by someone from the opposing team

Combat continues until one model loses its last wound or until three rounds are completed, all three rounds are played before moving to the next turn. At that point determine outcome:

If the Hero defeated the shadow they choose an eligible reward from Morr and are placed in the exit area standing up in spot that indicates they were successful

If the Hero loses their last wound, place them on their back in the exit area

If both models are standing, the Hero failed but is placed in the exit area standing up

Models are on their own in this fight and do not benefit from any terrain specific skills (no pitfighter bonus) or spells cast by another model that have an area effect, but any spells that are directly applicable to the model and haven’t expired are still in effect and are not mirrored by the shadow. Similarly “Favor of the Gods” cards do not affect combat in the Netherworld. Note: for the purposes of shooting, the Hero starts the combat stationary and so will not suffer a movement penalty if they don’t move on their turn. Also any special equipment such as poisons or magical artifacts will not be possessed by the shadow.

Returning from the Netherworld

Heroes in the Netherworld will return to the mortal realm at the start of the player’s next recovery phase. Successful Heroes can be placed anywhere within 6” of the temple (or inside the temple) but can’t be placed into close combat. Unsuccessful Heroes will return in a random position just outside the temple (use a direction die to determine location). Heroes on their back count as knocked down (can’t use leadership for route check) and recover as normal during recovery phase. Unsuccessful heroes that are standing are also returned to a random position but can be used for route check and can run, charge as normal.
scenarios.victory:
Ending the game

Due to the blood lust inspired by Morr, warbands will not involuntarily route, but may still choose to route if in route check. The game ends after 9 total successful petitions (8 for 3- and 6 for 2-player games), or if one side voluntarily routes. The winner will be determined by points: one point for each favor, 3 points for each normal shadow defeated, 6 points for each advanced shadow, and -5 points for routing. The winning side earns 4 extra favors, one extra auto-recovery (see After Action), and can make another petition see below. Note: either side can exchange unused favors for 5 gc each.
scenarios.experience:
Experience

+ 2 Survives. Heroes and Henchmen gain +2 XP for surviving

+1 Winning Leader. The leader of the winning warband gains +1 extra Experience

+1 Per Enemy Out of Action. A Hero earns +1 XP for each enemy model he puts out of action

+2 Normal shadow defeated. Heroes earn +2 XP for defeating a normal shadow and gaining a reward

+3 Advanced shadow defeated, Heroes earn +3 XP for defeating an advanced shadow
scenarios.rewards:
Rewards of the NetherLord

Each Hero can only receive one reward from the Netherlord. In addition, each warband can only have one reward from each category (normal and advanced are considered the same for this).

Opponent | Retrieve Henchman | Heal Injuries | Blood Chits | Amulet of Life
Normal | 1  H enchman | 1  H ealing potion | 6  Blood Chits | 1  Amulet  (4+)
Advanced | 2   H enchmen | 2   H ealing potions | 12  Blood Chits | 2   Amulet s (4+)

Any henchmen returned will have all the weapons/armor they had when they died. If fewer henchmen have died than are retrieved, a henchman (or two) of the player‘s choice is returned (no large models) with one single-handed weapon that they are eligible to use. Henchmen join the warband after the game and can either join an existing henchman group if the player supplies them with same weapons/equipment (same as deserter) or form a new group.

The healing potions can be used at any point after the game or after future games to heal one permanent injury to a Hero or to convert a henchman after-action roll to the next higher result, i.e. from “death” to “miss next game/lose all equipment” or from “miss next game” to full recovery

Blood chits can be distributed among the player’s Heroes after the game as desired

The 4+ amulet of life can be given to any model after the game

Final Petition

Each winning warband can send one hero (not taken out) to petition for a reward after the game. The warband may send a hero with a previous successful petition if no others are available and may double up on a category (normal only) if they have already received rewards in all four categories at no extra cost. If any Hero petitioning after the game is unsuccessful, roll a D6. If the Hero is knocked down, on a roll of 1-2 they are considered TOA for the game, if standing, on a roll of 1 they are considered TOA.
scenarios.aftermath:
After Action

All warbands will roll twice for each injury and choose which result to apply. Every unsuccessful petition earns an additional reroll. Every normal shadow defeated yields an automatic full recovery and every advanced shadow defeated yields two auto recoveries. These are applied at the end after all injury rolls (and initial rerolls) are completed but cannot be saved for later games.

If a warband does not have room for the returning henchman or if they choose not to retain any new henchmen, they can keep any weapons/armor the henchman had (or the one weapon the new henchman returned with) and they will receive ½ the cost of the henchman (rounded up) and +1 gc for each experience (or +4 gc for a new henchman) instead.

scenarios.name: The Valhalla Barracks
scenarios.narrative: Fluff: As warbands search the ruins of Mordheim for wyrdstone, they chance across a quarter of the city filled with barracks. In its former glory, the empire had built the barracks to house the many races in its army. To minimize the fighting between races, and also to keep the ghouls from eating the living, the empire had built a barracks for each race. Most of the barracks are looted hovels not worth searching again. In the distance, one set of barracks though is in fine shape with the barracks placard still intact. They approach it to take a closer look. When they near, they momentarily see the wording "Valhalla" and are hurtled into the barracks. They discover that this is the barracks of the Norse and they are in Valhalla.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain

Terrain is set up prior to players' arrival. As part of the terrain, Odin and Thor are waiting to bestow honor on worthy heroes. Denote the location of Odin and Thor with two 2" diameter markers in a line between two table edges and 8" from the table center (=14" edge-to-edge). Buildings are placed so that large boulevards run the length of the table between the deployment zones.
scenarios.deployment:
Warbands

There are two player teams and Odin. Since, Valhalla is a place for honored warriors, Empire deserters are not used in this scenario.

Warband Deployment

Warband deployment counts as resurrection into Valhalla (i.e. at the start of the game, all models get one 15" move). Each team rolls a 1d6 -- high roll sets up first -- choose Odin or Thor -- your deployment zone is on the table edge furthest from him. The other team deploys the opposite table edge. Teams set up within 10" of their table edge. Alternative 'deployment zones' are 4"x9" regions on each table edge 24" between each warband.

Turn Order

The teams roll for turn order -- high roll goes first. Odin goes last.
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

Valhalla

Fluff: Valhalla is the training ground of the Norse as they await Ragnarok, the final battle. Odin, the king of the gods, conjured Valhalla so that his warriors can hone their skills and gain combat experience. When a warrior falls at Valhalla, Valkyries fly to the fallen warrior and carry him to the warbands deployment area. In flight, powerful sorcerers resuscitate the fallen warrior. He lands whole and ready for battle once again. You have joined the Norse in their preparation for Ragnarok.

Odin's Favors: Through the ages, Odin has defeated countless heroes and looted their lifeless corpses. He keenly understands how to vanquish foes. In a feast after the battle, he bestows experience to warriors at Valhalla, in measure equal to their honor.

Honor and Glory

At the end of each close combat phase, if any hero or henchman has 2 or more ToA, Odin immediately plucks him from the field and sends him to the Hall of Glory for the remainder of the battle. After the battle, good things happen in the Hall of Glory.

Odin's Honor Sigils

Heroes can have honor bestowed on them by Odin or Thor. They do so by ending a movement phase in base-to-base contact with them. To denote the honor, the hero is given an Honor Sigil.

Only at the start of the game and after resurrection, heroes can receive an Honor Sigil from Odin/Thor furthest from their deployment zone.

Heroes can carry an unlimited number of Honor Sigils.

Heroes that are frenzied may choose to move (not run) to their statue (Odin or Thor) instead of a mandatory charge.  The model must be able to reach the statue with a normal move otherwise they must do a mandatory charge.

Resurrection

When a warrior falls at Valhalla, Valkyries immediately swoop in to carry the fallen warrior away.

In Odin's turn, models are automatically resurrected with full stats, and no magic buffs.

Models are resurrected either in their team's deployment zone or in an alternate deployment zone (player's choice).

Resurrected models are placed on the board at the beginning of their warband's turn.

Looking for redemption, on the turn they are resurrected, in lieu of their regular movement, models can choose to execute one 15" charge or move.
scenarios.victory:
Ending the game

The game ends when either time expires or if all models on a team are in the the Hall of Glory. If ended by time, the Bergermeister will announce the end of the game with sufficient time for the round to be played out and Odin conduct a final resurrection of models.

Additionally, in the after-action

Heroes in the Hall of Glory receive an additional Honor Sigil.

Henchmen and hired swords in the Hall of Glory receive a Battle Coup.

Each model (hero, henchmen, and hired sword) receives a Battle Coup for each hero they took out of action.

Winning the game

Winning the scenario is based on team Victory Points. The winner is the team with the most points. If tied, the game is a tie. Teams receive

1 Victory Point for each Honor Sigil that made it to the Hall of Glory (model carrying Honor Sigil was sent to the Hall of Glory)

1 Victory Point for each enemy model ToA
scenarios.experience:
Experience

+2 Survives. If a Hero or a Henchman group survives the battle they gain +2 Experience.

+1 Winning Leader. The leader of the winning warband gains +1 extra Experience.

+1 per Honor Sigil. Heroes earn +1 Exp for each Honor Sigil that made it to the Hall of Glory.

+1 per ToA. Heroes earn +1 Exp for each ToA.

+1 per Henchmen Battle Coup. Henchmen groups and hired swords earn +1 Exp for each Battle Coup obtained by taking a hero out of action. (max 3 per group)
scenarios.rewards:
The Loot

Warbands roll as normal for wyrdstone. Additionally, warbands may have Odin's Favor:

Each warband receives the sum of the team's Honor Sigils.

Each warband receives the sum of the team's Battle Coups.

Winning warbands get their choice of either +5 Honor Sigils or +5 Battle Coups.

Players then pair their Honor Sigils and Battle Coups. Specifically, 1x (Honor Sigil + Battle Coup) = one Imbued Battle Coup. The player can use Imbued Battle Coups to increase hero's experience.

Teams can use a maximum of 10 Imbued Battle Coups.

Players can exchange each Imbued Battle Coup for +1 Experience.

Nominate a warband hero -- that hero gets plus one experience. Experience has to be evenly distributed amongst all warband heroes, i.e. no hero may get a second experience plus up until all heroes have one.

• Remaining Honor Sigils and Battle Coups can be exchanged for 2gc each.

Example 1: A player has 6 Honor Sigils and 9 Battle Coups. The warband receives +6 Exp to distribute amongst its heroes +6g.

Example 2: A player has 6 Honor Sigils and 4 Battle Coups. The warband receives +4 Exp to distribute amongst its heroes +4g.
