scenarios.name: The Corbomite Wands
scenarios.narrative:
(This is a variant of the rulebook's Bounty Hunt scenario.)

Fluff: Recently, warbands breached the ramparts of a great palace. In ceremonial display cases throughout the palace grounds, they find ornately inscribed wands -- they loot them, of course, and continue on their way. Two such warbands find themselves on opposite ends of a backstreet alley.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain

Terrain is set up prior to player's arrival in a manner typical for a Street Fight scenario.
scenarios.deployment:
Warband deployment

Each team rolls a dice -- high roll sets up first. The first player chooses a street edge and places his warriors within 8" of that edge -- his opponent then sets up within 8" of the opposite edge.

All six heroes from each warband are equipped with Corbomite Wands, two of each type -- give the heroes colored pipe cleaners to denote the wands. If the warband has less than six heroes, give a wand to henchmen (no animals).

Starting the Game

Both teams roll a D6 -- the higher scoring team takes the first turn.
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

Corbomite Wands

Corbomite items are enchanted items, which have then been inscribed with runes. In an ancient elven workshop, rune masters fashioned corbomite wands by inscribing wands with runes that read: "Do onto others as they will do to you". Only two wands from each warband can be activated per turn.

At the beginning of their magic phase, a warband can activate two wands. The use of the wands is as an extra action in that phase.

Corbomite wands have a single spell bound to them -- on use of the wand, that spell is auto-cast.

On use of a wand, a wand of the opponent's choosing simultaneously auto-casts its spell. Specifically: (1) a player activates a wand and declares a target, (2) his opponents choose a wand and declare a target, (3) the primary cast is worked out, (4) the mirror cast is worked out.

Example 1: A Noble activates a Wand of Teleport and nominates a Troll Slayer. His opponents choose 'Wand of

Teleport' carried by a Vampire and nominate a dreg. The Troll Slayer is teleported, then the dreg is

teleported.

Example 2: An Engineer activates his Wand of Recovery and nominates the captain. His opponents choose 'Wand of

Arha' carried by a BigUn and nominates Hench_1. The dwarve captain stands up, then the Arrows of

Arha are fired at Hench_1.

Example 3: A Necromancer activates his Wand of Teleport and nominates Hench_2. His opponents choose 'Wand

of Arha' carried by a Jarl and also nominate Hench_2. Hench_2 is teleported out of LOS --> the Jarl

cannot shoot the arrows of Arha.

When a wand bearer is ToA, the wand becomes inert and is picked up by the opposing warband.

The Wands in Play

(Blue) Corbomite Wand of Recovery Nominate a friendly model that is knocked down or stunned -- that model stands up. (Treat the model as standing up in this Recovery Phase.)

(Green) Corbomite Wand of Teleportation Nominate a friendly model within 12" -- that model is teleported ≤6" (LOS applies). The model cannot be placed in, or removed from, BtB.

(White) Corbomite Wand of Arha Silver Arrows of Arha with D2 arrows.  The arrows have a range of 24”, are S3, hit on a 4+, and do not cause critical hits.
scenarios.victory:
Ending the game

The game ends when either both warbands on a team fail their route tests, or when all wand bearers on a team are ToA. A team wins if it ToAs 6 or more wand bearers. A team loses if it ToAs 2 or less wand bearers.  If neither team ToAs 6 or more wand bearers, then the winner is determined by the team which best fulfilled the scenario objectives (at the discretion of the Burgomeister).  If one team loses based on ToAs of wand bearers, then the other team automatically wins.

Route checks in this scenario are taken at: Leadership + (# ToA this round) + (# bounties)
scenarios.experience:
After-action Experience

+1 Survives. If a Hero or a Henchman group survives the battle, they gain +2 Exp.

+1 Winning Leaders. The leaders of the winning team gain +1 Exp.

+1 Per ToA. Heroes earn +1 Exp for each enemy model or guardian they ToA.

+1 for Risk. Heroes carrying a wand earn +1 additional Experience if they have at least 1 ToA.

+1 Per Bounty. Heroes and henchmen groups earn +1 Exp for each enemy wand bearer they ToA.
scenarios.rewards:
The Treasure

Rolling for wyrdstone: Warbands get one D6 die for each hero that survives plus the number found in the treasure vault. (Remember you can only keep a maximum of 6 dice when you roll for Wyrdstone.)

Each warband gets the sum of the team's looted wands. Winning warbands get one additional wand.

In after-action looting, warbands discover Count Steinhart's Treasure Vault. They also discover that inert wands, i.e. those that have been looted from ToA heroes, have the ability to unlock drawers in the vault—the more wands that are required to open a drawer, the better the loot. The drawers are well labeled and there are many drawers with each label.

scenarios.name: The Rich Quarter
scenarios.narrative: While undoubtedly the Rich Quarter has seen better days, and even years, there is still a great deal that has not been pillaged within this sector. One such near pristine, for Mordheim at least, is the area surrounding the estates of Baron Hieronymus Karl Friedrich. Shortly after the Empire retook control of Mordheim the Baron’s heirs, as well as other nobles who had interests there, insisted that something be done about the looting of their estates. An order came down from the Emperor himself that any looters, be they military or mercenary, are to be executed. In the first couple of years there were several soldiers executed for such activity. Now patrols are always conducted with more senior personal, the only people being executed nowadays are unlucky scavengers. As far as Mordheim goes, this is about as pristine as it gets.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain:

At the center of this block is the once great manor of Baron Hieronymus Karl Friedrich, a ruined hovel compared to its former splendor. Surrounding it are various outbuildings that were kept for frequent guests and their retinue and even some shops that once specifically catered to the rich.

There should be a large, some-what open building in the center of the table to represent the Baron’s Manor House.
scenarios.deployment:
Setup:

There will be 12 treasure tokens, 8 Lesser tokens, 4 greater tokens. The 4 Greater and 4 of the lesser tokens will be randomly placed 10” from the center of the Manor house on each of the 8 directional points. If in a street, consider it hidden in some rubble or the remains of a fallen looter from the past. (Perhaps Barrels or such be placed nearby)

The last 4 lesser tokens will be placed 16” from the center building at Diagonals (Ie, 2,4,6,8 directions)

Warbands:

Each team rolls a die. Winner chooses which side they wish to enter from and starts setup. Teams ‘split’ their side, not allowing for intermingling at the start, they must all start on the ground floor within 8” of the table edge. The losing team of this roll then has the opposite side and sets up similar. Roll a die to see who acts first.

Starting the game:

Each Warband rolls a D6, winner chooses a side and sets up within 8” of their table edge. The loser sets up afterwards on the opposite table edge. Warbands cannot be intermingled, as such, split table edge in half for each warband/Mercenary group.
scenarios.rules:

Baron Friedrich’s Manor:

There is a large pile of treasure within this Manor, collected and guarded by a Demon. Merely entering this building will get the Demon’s attention. At the end of all player’s turns after someone has entered the Manor House, roll 1d4 to determine which Demon is present and act accordingly.

Demon’s Actions

The Demon will appear near whoever is closest to the treasure (center of building) and immediately attack

Due to the demon’s attachment to the treasure, he is aware of any and all models within the mansion.

The Demon’s subsequent turns will be Semi Random: Roll 1d6. 1-2: Demon acts after all player turns, 3-4: Demon acts between the turns of Team 1 and Team 2, 5-6: Demon acts first.

Demon’s Turn:

The Demon will randomly attack one of the three closest models to him. If he charges outside of the building, he will continue this method based upon those closest to him.

Players turn:

When striking back, the demon will randomly attack whoever is in close combat and focus all attacks on them, even knocked down or stunned models are counted in the random determination, at which point they will violate the normal rule preventing attacking a downed model when engaged with other models.

No attackable models.

If at any time there are no chargeable models, the Demon fades away, back to guard his treasure, if models in there, he immediately remanifests as if the first time. (lost wounds remain lost)

Infiltration: Infiltrators have half again the usual penalty (18”) when trying to set up, due to the difficulties of avoiding the patrols to enter in the first place. And may not start in contact with a ‘treasure token’. An Infiltrator who is in the manor house automatically awakens the Demon.

Searching: A Hero model must end its turn on a Token to begin searching/looting, searching and events do not occur until the end of that players turn. If a 1-2 is rolled on the search, in addition to any loot you will encounter a hazard. Roll 1D6 and consult your doom. If a Greater treasure marker is pulled, the chance of an event is raised to 1-3 on a 6 sided die. Loot is determined at the end of the game.

Guards: Guards will try to assault the warband they found looting as a priority, no warband may have more than one patrol after them at any given time, as such, subsequent rolls of 1 will only spawn reinforcements up to their original patrol size. There could be as many as 4 guard patrols, each after a different Warband.

The Hero Searching Makes an initiative check at -2, if successful you jump to a safe spot, if not, they take  D3 S4 hits, no armor saves, any others within the building make an initiative check as normal(Or within 3” of a street token) take D2 S4 hits, no armor saves.

If successful, you avoid the resulting ball of fire that explodes, if failed take D3 S3 hits, no armor saves for each model affected. If you are flammable, +1 Strength of the hit.

scenarios.name: The Wizard’s Stash
scenarios.narrative: A crazed old man has been wandering through base camp claiming that the renowned wizard, Milo Snorley, never left Mordheim.  It was rumored that Milo stayed in the city after the comet, accumulating wealth and treasures from the abandoned homes of the rich.  Unfortunately, the Wyrdstone poison drove him mad and he hung himself in the city square.  To date, no one has found Milo’s stash.  The crazed old man tells you he believes it is in the River Gate Tower, which still stands.  He is certain it is there, but he is afraid to investigate it as Milo was known for crafting magical traps.  You quickly eliminate the crazed old man before he tells others his tale, and plan to visit the tower during your next raid into Mordheim.
scenarios.terrain:
Terrain

Create a wall with a tower and two Giant Crossbows as shown below.  Place buildings as normal to the inside of the wall.  Ensure there are plenty of paths via bridges between the buildings, and between the buildings and the wall.  Warbands/teams start in the designated Start Zones which are 4”x24” each.  Warbands on the same team may intermix in the Start Zone.
scenarios.deployment:
Placing Models

Roll for sides, place models, and then roll for turn.  Warbands setup within their designated Start Zone, and warbands on a team may intermix their models.
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

Muddy

There was a large rainstorm over night, and the neglected streets of Mordheim have turned to mud.  All models on the ground floor, and not inside a building, are considered to be in difficult terrain (half movement).

Giant Crossbows

The Giant Crossbows were created by the wizards of Mordheim to help protect the city.  Each Giant Crossbow is loaded, but can only be fired once.  Any hero may end their regular movement in base contact with a Giant Crossbow.  A hero that starts their turn in base contact with a Giant Crossbow and does not move during their movement phase, may fire the Giant Crossbow during their shooting phase.

The Giant Crossbows have a range of 48” and a strength of 6.  The magical sights created by the wizards can see through all terrain so the Giant Crossbows can be fired at any model on the table (including hidden models).  The bolts of the Giant Crossbows will go through most anything.  When the Giant Crossbow is fired, draw a line from the crossbow, through the target (target must be an enemy model, line goes through the chest of the target model), and on until the bolt leaves the table or impacts the ground.  The bolt will hit/go through every model (if it passes over the models base at less than or equal to standard height of that type of model – you get no benefit for a crouching model) and piece of terrain in its path.  For each piece of terrain the bolt passes through, roll a d6.  On a roll of 1-2, the bolt loses 1 strength.  For each model the bolt passes through, roll a d6.  On a roll of 3-6, the bolt hits the target at its current strength, and causes a critical hit on a roll of 5-6.  Each successful “wound” from the bolt causes two wounds to the model.

Milo Snorley’s Stash

Milo Snorley’s stash is hidden in the upper floor of the corner tower.  Any model may enter the upper floor of the tower, but only heroes can grab from the stash.  Each model that enters the upper floor of the tower risks triggering one of Milo’s magical traps (see below).  Place 7 treasure tokens (numbered 1-7) in the upper floor of the tower.  Heroes that end their movement phase in the upper floor of the tower, and do not shoot, cast spells, or engage in close combat, may select one of the remaining treasure tokens carry it for the remainder of the scenario.  If a hero carrying a treasure token is knocked down, stunned, or taken out of action, the token is dropped and scatters d3” in a random direction.  Any hero which ends their regular movement (not a charge) in base contact with a dropped treasure token may pick it up.  No hero may carry more than one token at a time.

The seven treasure tokens are:

1.  Gems

2.  Armor

3.  Book

4.  Weapon

5.  Wyrdstone

6.  Missile Weapon

7.  Artifact

Magical Traps

When a model enters the upper floor of the corner tower, roll a d6 to see if they trigger a magical trap.  On a roll of 1-4, a trap is triggered.  If a trap is triggered, roll an additional d6.  On a roll of 1-3, the trap is a fireball.  On a roll of 4-6, the trap is a lightning bolt.  The fireball automatically hits all models within 2” of the model which triggered the trap causing a Strength 3 hit.  The lightning bolt automatically hits the model which triggered the trap causing a Strength 5 hit.  If the lightning bolt successfully wounds the target model, it jumps to the nearest model within 3” of the target which has not been hit by the lightning bolt.  Whenever the lightning bolt jumps, it loses 1 strength.  As long as the lightning bolt successfully wounds its target, it will continue to jump as long as there is another valid target.  The lightning bolt will not jump back to a previous target.
scenarios.victory:
Ending the game

The game ends when one team has completely routed.
scenarios.experience:
Experience

+1 Survives. If a Hero or a Henchman group survives the battle they gain +1 Experience.

+1 Winning Leader. The leader of a winning warband gains +1 extra Experience.

+1 Per Enemy Out of Action. Any Hero earns +1 Experience for each enemy model he puts out of action.

+1 Risk Bonus.  Any Hero that retrieved a token from the tower gains an additional +1 Experience.
scenarios.rewards:
Milo Snorley’s Treasure

Warbands keep any treasure tokens they are holding at the end of the game.  Treasure tokens which were dropped during the scenario but not picked up are lost in the mud and debris of Mordheim.  After the game ends, any heroes on the winning team which were not taken out of action and are not carrying a token may enter the tower to retrieve unclaimed tokens.  To do this, the winning team must first declare which heroes are entering the tower.  Place them in a line, 1.25” apart from each other.  Starting with the lead hero, roll a d6 for each hero, one at a time.  On a roll of 1-4, the hero has triggered a trap.  Resolve the trap before rolling for the next hero. Any hero that survives the traps may collect one of the treasure tokens remaining in the tower.

For each token a warband/team collected, they roll below based on the token number.  When playing with teams, roll once for the team and each warband of the team receives the item.  The winning team adds 2d6 to the roll for item 1 (Gems), and adds +1 to the die rolls for items 2-7.

1.  Gems.  The gems can be sold for 3d6 gold.

2.  Armor:  Roll 2d6.  2-6 Useless, 7-8 Light Armor, 9-10 Heavy Armor, 11-12 Ithilmar Shield.  The Ithilmar shield is very light.  It provides armor saves as per a normal shield, does not create a -1M penalty when combined with heavy armor, and can also parry.  The Ithilmar shield may be sold for 20gc.

3.  Book.  Roll 2d6.  2-7 Useless, 8-9 Mordheim Map, 10-11 Hafling Cookbook, 12 Tome of Magic/Holy Tome (player’s choice).

4.  Weapon.  Roll 2d6.  2-7 Single hand weapon (common, player’s choice), 8-10 Ithilmar Weapon (single hand, common, player’s choice), 11-12 Gromril Weapon (single hand, common, player’s choice).

5.  Wyrdstone.  D6-3 (min 1) shards of wyrdstone.

6.  Missile Weapon.  2-5 Bow, 6-7 Long Bow, 8-9 Crossbow, 10-11 Crossbow Pistol, 12 Repeating Crossbow.

7.  Artifact.  2-7 Useless, 8-10 Holy/Unholy Relic, 11-12 Ring +1 Movement.

scenarios.name: Temple of Sigmar
scenarios.narrative: The once great temple district has fallen in time. The center of the area you have come upon lies the Temple of Sigmar. Guards rarely come in these parts due to the even rarer event of them returning. Little is known except that there is life amongst, and some say within, the stone. The reality is truer than they can believe.
scenarios.deployment:
Setup:

One building in center of table representing temple, then normal terrain. Statues (which need not be represented), both whole and broken litter the entire temple district

Starting the Game

Each team rolls a die. Winning player can decide which side and must set up first.

Each team will roll again to determine who goes first.
scenarios.rules:
Maps, diagrams and original table layout are available in the linked original document. Special rules and awards are resolved manually.

Special Rules:

Infiltration:

A model may not start inside the Temple using Infiltration or similar abilities.

Temple Protection:

A model within the structure of the temple, as per our rules regarding how pit-fighters work), may choose to be an invalid target for the purposes of placing a statue on them.

Temple District:

This region is filled with Statues, both whole and pieces, seemingly out of place throughout the middle of the streets and buildings.

Statues: Statues come to life periodically.  These are empowered by the essense of Sigmar, and other gods, their sole purpose to test to see who is worthy or not.

At the end of each round:

All statues cease to be animated, effectively disappearing from combat.

A model that just had a statue engaged with them last round may not be targeted.

The opposing players will determine which model of that warband to place a statue on, which counts as charging. The Statue must charge a standing unengaged figurine. They may choose whether that statue charges their warband, or the warband that generated the statue.

Each player rolls 2d6 to determine what their test will be: 2-6 Lesser Statue, 7-8 Normal Statue, 9-10: Greater Statue, 11-12: Hero of Sigmar. And place it in the model that was nominated by the opposing player, this actions counts as charging and initiates a close combat round.

Any Model taken out of action by a Statue has a Full recovery

For every 2 models taken out by the statues, it counts as only 1 out of action for losses (Think Goblins in Orcs, and yes this means 4 goblins taken out by statues would count as 1)

Deserters: The Statues will not target filthy deserters, also, the deserters want nothing to do with the statues, they will not attack with range or charge the statues, if one ends up in base to base contact with a statue somehow, they will die.

Enemies:

scenarios.victory:
Ending the Game:

The game ends when either time runs out, or both warbands on a side have routed.

Winning the game:

Winning the game is decided entirely on Victory points.

Deserter out of action: 0pts

Henchmen taken out of action: 1pt

Hero Taken out of action: 2pt

Lesser statue taken out of action: 0pt

Normal Statue taken out of action: 0pt*

Greater Statue taken out of action: 1pt*

Hero of Sigmar Taken out of action: 3pt*

*For normal or greater statues, you get +1pt if the statue is taken out solo, ie, by the model it charged, or if a single model counter-charged if the statue killed its target on the turn it charged.

Being in route check: -1pt

Warband Routed: -2pt

Both warbands routed: -5pt
